title: The King and the Elephant (मराठी)
summary: A rogue elephant refuses to move, blocking the palace gates. Birbal moves the giant beast without an iron hook or whip. [MR]
full_text:
A massive imperial tusker named Gajraj, known for his formidable size in battle, suddenly became stubborn and obstinate. Right in front of the main Hathipol (Elephant Gate) of the Agra Fort, the colossal elephant sat down across the stone road, folded his thick legs, and refused to budge.

Caravans, horsemen, and royal messengers were completely blocked. The mahouts beat the beast with iron ankus (hooks), yelled curses, and set off firecrackers, but Gajraj merely flapped his ears, trumpeted angrily, and planted his massive bulk even firmer into the dust.

Akbar stood on the ramparts, frustrated: 'Bring the royal cavalry! Tie twenty chains to his legs and pull him with forty horses!'

Birbal arrived and observed the scene. 'Sire, pulling a five-ton stubborn elephant with chains will only injure the beast and break our horses' backs. Force cannot conquer stubbornness; one must appeal to nature.'

Birbal walked to the palace kitchens. He returned carrying three large wicker baskets filled with fresh, juicy pineapples, sweet jaggery cakes, and tender green sugarcane stalks.

Birbal walked calmly to within twenty paces of the sitting elephant. He peeled a sweet pineapple, letting the rich, sugary aroma drift into the morning breeze.

Gajraj's trunk sniffed the air. The elephant's ears perked up.

Birbal placed a jaggery cake on the grass fifteen paces down the side road. Gajraj's trunk curled. Slowly, groaning with delight, the massive beast uncurled his legs, stood up on all fours, and ambled peacefully off the main road to eat the sweet treat!

Birbal walked ahead, dropping pieces of sugarcane every few paces, leading the docile giant gently into his stable paddock, where the gates were closed securely behind him.

The main roadway was completely clear within ten minutes, without a single blow struck!

Akbar cheered from the ramparts: 'Brilliant, Birbal! You moved with three sugar cakes what twenty iron hooks could not budge!'

Birbal smiled: 'Sire, whether dealing with stubborn beasts or rebellious citizens, sweetness and understanding lead where anger and whips only harden resistance.'

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The King and the Elephant"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
